prediction: The Federal Housing Administration (FHA) insures private mortgage lenders against borrower default, enabling access to affordable mortgages for first-time and lower-income homebuyers. FHA-insured mortgages have lower down payment requirements and more lenient credit standards compared to conventional mortgages. FHA plays a countercyclical role, insuring more mortgages during economic downturns. FHA's market share fluctuates with economic conditions, peaking at over 30% of home purchase mortgages during the 2007-2009 housing crisis. The FHA Mutual Mortgage Insurance Fund (MMI Fund) is funded through insurance premiums and proceeds from foreclosed properties. While the fund has historically generated negative credit subsidies, it has faced challenges with low capital ratios. Recent reforms, including higher down payments for lower credit scores, have strengthened the fund. FHA insures over 8 million single-family mortgages, with a total outstanding balance of nearly $1.2 trillion as of FY2018.
